items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: Gossum, a fella called Gossum was giving them picnics out there.

ctx.x: You were speaking about Freddie Kepard earlier. What kind of a style? Was he any different to the other trumpet players? No, no.

He played that Dixieland and jazz trumpet just like the rest of them. Yeah. They all have to play that same way, you see, when you play the trumpet. Because when you get in a band, if you're playing trumpet in a band like they was playing then, you'd have to play that style, you know? The only difference was some fellas could play in brass band music and they couldn't play dance music, you see. That's the two different types of music, you see. When there's a straight and a jazz the other way to dance and music,…

Well, I read Piku told us something about playing out there too with Manuel Perez. Oh, yeah, yeah. I played with Piku out there too. Piku said he remembers the same time when Freddie picked up the cornet sometime.
